description: Build a rare and valuable skill stack by rating your skills honestly, finding an unusual combination that meets a market need, and investing in the weakest link.

steps.description: List your current skills and the candidate skills you could realistically develop.

inputs.name: background-summary
inputs.desc: A short summary of your work history and projects

inputs.name: interest-areas
inputs.desc: Areas you are drawn to or want to grow into

outputs.name: skill-inventory
outputs.desc: A grouped list of skills you currently use

outputs.name: candidate-skill-list
outputs.desc: Skills you could realistically develop within a year or two

process: List every skill you currently use in work or projects, grouped by type.
Add candidate skills you could realistically reach within a year or two.
Record each skill with a short note on how you use or would use it.
Separate skills tied to your interest areas from the rest.

steps.description: Rate your honest percentile standing in each skill against the people who use it professionally.

inputs.name: skill-inventory
inputs.desc: A grouped list of skills you currently use

inputs.name: candidate-skill-list
inputs.desc: Skills you could realistically develop within a year or two

outputs.name: percentile-ratings
outputs.desc: An honest percentile estimate for each skill

outputs.name: top-quartile-skills
outputs.desc: Skills where you sit in or could reach the top quartile

process: For each skill, estimate your percentile against people who use it professionally.
Base the estimate on evidence such as results, feedback, or comparison.
Flag any skill where you sit in the top quartile or could reach it.
Separate skills that are already strong from skills that still need work.

steps.description: Find unusual combinations of two or three skills that few people hold together.

inputs.name: percentile-ratings
inputs.desc: An honest percentile estimate for each skill

inputs.name: top-quartile-skills
inputs.desc: Skills where you sit in or could reach the top quartile

outputs.name: candidate-combinations
outputs.desc: Candidate pairings and triples of your stronger skills

outputs.name: rarity-notes
outputs.desc: An estimate of how rare each combination is

process: Pair and triple your stronger skills to form candidate combinations.
Estimate how rare each combination is among people in your field.
Keep combinations that are both rare and plausible for you to own.
Note the one skill in each combination that makes it distinctive.

steps.description: Test each candidate combination against a real market need to find the strongest fit.

inputs.name: candidate-combinations
inputs.desc: Candidate pairings and triples of your stronger skills

inputs.name: rarity-notes
inputs.desc: An estimate of how rare each combination is

outputs.name: market-matched-combinations
outputs.desc: Combinations matched to the needs they could serve

outputs.name: fit-rationale
outputs.desc: The reasoning behind the chosen combination

process: List the market needs or problems you could serve with each combination.
Score each combination on demand, your access to it, and competition.
Select the combination with the strongest market fit.
Write the rationale so you can revisit the choice later.

steps.description: Identify the weakest skill in the chosen stack, since raising it lifts the whole stack.

inputs.name: market-matched-combinations
inputs.desc: Combinations matched to the needs they could serve

inputs.name: fit-rationale
inputs.desc: The reasoning behind the chosen combination

outputs.name: priority-skill
outputs.desc: The weakest skill in the chosen stack to improve first

outputs.name: improvement-targets
outputs.desc: Specific targets that define better for that skill

process: Compare the skills inside the chosen combination by current percentile.
Select the weakest skill, since raising it lifts the whole stack.
Define specific improvement targets for that skill.
Confirm the targets are observable and checkable.

steps.description: Produce an investment roadmap for building the chosen skill stack over time.

inputs.name: priority-skill
inputs.desc: The weakest skill in the chosen stack to improve first

inputs.name: improvement-targets
inputs.desc: Specific targets that define better for that skill

outputs.name: skill-stack-roadmap
outputs.desc: A sequenced plan for building the stack

outputs.name: review-schedule
outputs.desc: A schedule for re-rating percentiles and adjusting

process: Sequence the skills to develop, starting with the priority skill.
Set time allocations and milestones for each skill.
Schedule reviews to re-rate percentiles and adjust the stack.
Record the roadmap and the first action to take this week.

description: Design a deliberate practice routine that targets a specific weakness at the edge of your ability, isolates the sub-skill, builds in immediate feedback, and adjusts over cycles.

steps.description: Turn a broad goal into one specific sub-skill to practice at the edge of your ability.

inputs.name: broad-goal
inputs.desc: The general ability you want to improve

inputs.name: current-level
inputs.desc: A description of your current performance

outputs.name: target-sub-skill
outputs.desc: One specific sub-skill stated as an observable behavior

outputs.name: ability-edge-note
outputs.desc: A note on where this sits at the edge of your ability

process: State the broad goal, then break it into component sub-skills.
Pick one sub-skill that is just beyond your current reliable performance.
Write the target as an observable, specific behavior rather than a vague aim.
Confirm the target is narrow enough to practice in isolation.

steps.description: Design a focused task that isolates the target sub-skill and repeats it many times.

inputs.name: target-sub-skill
inputs.desc: One specific sub-skill stated as an observable behavior

inputs.name: ability-edge-note
inputs.desc: A note on where this sits at the edge of your ability

outputs.name: practice-task
outputs.desc: A task stripped down to the single sub-skill

outputs.name: repetition-plan
outputs.desc: How many focused repetitions fit one session

process: Strip the task down to the single sub-skill, removing unrelated steps.
Set the difficulty so success is uncertain but reachable.
Plan how many focused repetitions fit into one session.
Define what one clean repetition looks like start to finish.

steps.description: Build an immediate feedback source so each repetition is scored against a standard.

inputs.name: practice-task
inputs.desc: A task stripped down to the single sub-skill

inputs.name: repetition-plan
inputs.desc: How many focused repetitions fit one session

outputs.name: feedback-source
outputs.desc: The source that scores each repetition immediately

outputs.name: success-standard
outputs.desc: The standard that marks a repetition as correct

process: Define the standard that marks a repetition as correct.
Choose a feedback source that is immediate, such as a recording, a tool, a coach, or a checklist.
Decide how you will capture the result of each repetition.
Test that the feedback arrives fast enough to guide the next attempt.

steps.description: Plan a short, high-focus practice session with full attention and rest.

inputs.name: practice-task
inputs.desc: A task stripped down to the single sub-skill

inputs.name: feedback-source
inputs.desc: The source that scores each repetition immediately

outputs.name: session-plan
outputs.desc: A plan for one focused practice session

outputs.name: focus-rules
outputs.desc: Rules that remove distraction during the session

process: Set a session length short enough to sustain full concentration.
Schedule the session when your attention is highest.
Define rules that remove distraction during the session.
Plan short rest breaks between blocks of repetitions.

steps.description: Run the sessions and log performance against the standard for each repetition.

inputs.name: session-plan
inputs.desc: A plan for one focused practice session

inputs.name: success-standard
inputs.desc: The standard that marks a repetition as correct

outputs.name: practice-log
outputs.desc: A record of results across sessions

outputs.name: error-patterns
outputs.desc: The specific errors that recur across repetitions

process: Record the result of each repetition against the success standard.
Note the specific errors that recur across repetitions.
Track the success rate across sessions over time.
Mark the point where performance plateaus or improves.

steps.description: Review the log and adjust the target, difficulty, or feedback for the next cycle.

inputs.name: practice-log
inputs.desc: A record of results across sessions

inputs.name: error-patterns
inputs.desc: The specific errors that recur across repetitions

outputs.name: practice-adjustments
outputs.desc: Changes to make for the next cycle

outputs.name: next-cycle-plan
outputs.desc: The plan for the next practice cycle

process: Read the error patterns to find the next limiting sub-skill.
Raise difficulty when success is reliable, or lower it when progress stalls.
Adjust the feedback source if it is not catching the real errors.
Write the plan for the next practice cycle.

description: Learn a concept deeply by explaining it in plain language to a beginner, finding the gaps where you fall back on jargon, studying those gaps, and simplifying again.

steps.description: Choose the concept to learn and write down what you already know about it.

inputs.name: concept-name
inputs.desc: The concept or topic you want to understand

inputs.name: current-understanding
inputs.desc: What you already believe you know about it

outputs.name: concept-scope
outputs.desc: The concept framed as a clear question to answer

outputs.name: prior-knowledge-notes
outputs.desc: What you can state about it from memory

process: State the concept as a single clear question you want to answer.
Write everything you already know about it from memory.
Mark the boundary of what the explanation needs to cover.
List the parts you are least sure about.

steps.description: Explain the concept in plain language as if teaching a twelve-year-old.

inputs.name: concept-scope
inputs.desc: The concept framed as a clear question to answer

inputs.name: prior-knowledge-notes
inputs.desc: What you can state about it from memory

outputs.name: plain-explanation
outputs.desc: An explanation written in everyday words

outputs.name: analogy-list
outputs.desc: Analogies and examples that carry the idea

process: Write the explanation using only everyday words.
Replace technical terms with simple analogies and examples.
Keep each sentence focused on one idea.
Read it aloud to check a beginner could follow it.

steps.description: Scan the explanation for jargon and hand-waving that hide a lack of understanding.

inputs.name: plain-explanation
inputs.desc: An explanation written in everyday words

inputs.name: analogy-list
inputs.desc: Analogies and examples that carry the idea

outputs.name: jargon-flags
outputs.desc: Places where a technical term stood in for understanding

outputs.name: knowledge-gaps
outputs.desc: Specific questions to research

process: Mark every place where you used a technical term without explaining it.
Mark every place where the explanation jumps or feels vague.
Turn each flagged spot into a specific question to research.
Rank the questions by how central they are to the concept.

steps.description: Study the source material to fill the specific gaps that the explanation exposed.

inputs.name: jargon-flags
inputs.desc: Places where a technical term stood in for understanding

inputs.name: knowledge-gaps
inputs.desc: Specific questions to research

outputs.name: gap-research-notes
outputs.desc: Plain-language answers to each gap question

outputs.name: resolved-questions
outputs.desc: The questions you can now answer cleanly

process: Go back to the source material for each flagged question.
Study until you can answer the question in your own words.
Record the answer as a short, plain note.
Mark any question that is still unresolved for another pass.

steps.description: Rewrite the explanation, folding in the new understanding and cutting remaining jargon.

inputs.name: gap-research-notes
inputs.desc: Plain-language answers to each gap question

inputs.name: resolved-questions
inputs.desc: The questions you can now answer cleanly

outputs.name: simplified-explanation
outputs.desc: A clearer explanation with the gaps filled

outputs.name: refined-analogies
outputs.desc: Analogies improved by the new understanding

process: Rewrite the explanation using the resolved answers.
Replace any remaining jargon with a simpler phrasing or analogy.
Shorten sentences so each carries one idea.
Check the explanation now flows without a jump.

steps.description: Test the final explanation against a real listener and capture anything still unclear.

inputs.name: simplified-explanation
inputs.desc: A clearer explanation with the gaps filled

inputs.name: refined-analogies
inputs.desc: Analogies improved by the new understanding

outputs.name: verified-explanation
outputs.desc: The explanation after testing it on a listener

outputs.name: remaining-gaps
outputs.desc: Gaps to feed the next round of study

process: Explain the concept to another person or record yourself.
Note any question you could not answer cleanly.
List remaining gaps to feed the next round of study.
Decide whether the concept is understood well enough to stop.

description: Set up a spaced repetition system that turns material into recall prompts, schedules reviews at expanding intervals, and runs short daily sessions for long-term retention.

steps.description: Break the material into small, atomic facts and ideas worth remembering.

inputs.name: source-material
inputs.desc: The material you want to retain

inputs.name: retention-goal
inputs.desc: What you need to recall and why

outputs.name: atomic-items
outputs.desc: The smallest facts that stand on their own

outputs.name: priority-tags
outputs.desc: A priority and topic tag for each item

process: Split the material into the smallest facts that stand on their own.
Keep only items you genuinely need to recall from memory.
Tag each item by priority and topic.
Drop items that are better looked up than memorized.

steps.description: Turn each item into a question-and-answer prompt that forces active recall.

inputs.name: atomic-items
inputs.desc: The smallest facts that stand on their own

inputs.name: priority-tags
inputs.desc: A priority and topic tag for each item

outputs.name: recall-prompts
outputs.desc: Questions that force recall of one fact each

outputs.name: answer-keys
outputs.desc: The single clear answer for each prompt

process: Write each item as a question with a single, clear answer.
Keep each prompt focused on one fact to avoid interference.
Add a cue or context where the bare question is ambiguous.
Rewrite any prompt that could be answered without real recall.

steps.description: Assign an expanding review schedule such as one, three, seven, fourteen, thirty, and ninety days.

inputs.name: recall-prompts
inputs.desc: Questions that force recall of one fact each

inputs.name: answer-keys
inputs.desc: The single clear answer for each prompt

outputs.name: review-schedule
outputs.desc: The first review date for each prompt

outputs.name: interval-ladder
outputs.desc: The expanding ladder of review intervals

process: Set the expanding interval ladder for new items.
Assign each prompt a first review date.
Define how a correct answer moves an item up the ladder.
Define how an incorrect answer resets an item to a short interval.

steps.description: Plan a short daily review session that fits the due prompts into a fixed time box.

inputs.name: review-schedule
inputs.desc: The first review date for each prompt

inputs.name: interval-ladder
inputs.desc: The expanding ladder of review intervals

outputs.name: daily-session-plan
outputs.desc: A plan for the short daily review

outputs.name: due-queue-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for building each day's queue

process: Set a fixed daily time box of about fifteen minutes.
Define how due prompts are pulled into each day's queue.
Decide what happens when the queue is larger than the time box.
Pick a consistent time of day for the session.

steps.description: Run the daily sessions, scoring recall and updating each item's next interval.

inputs.name: daily-session-plan
inputs.desc: A plan for the short daily review

inputs.name: due-queue-rules
inputs.desc: Rules for building each day's queue

outputs.name: review-log
outputs.desc: A record of recall results over time

outputs.name: lapse-list
outputs.desc: Items that failed and need extra attention

process: Answer each due prompt from memory before checking the key.
Score each answer and move the item along or back on the ladder.
Add failed items to the lapse list for extra attention.
Stop when the time box ends and carry any overflow to tomorrow.

steps.description: Review the log, reset lapsed items, and tune the intervals for better retention.

inputs.name: review-log
inputs.desc: A record of recall results over time

inputs.name: lapse-list
inputs.desc: Items that failed and need extra attention

outputs.name: tuned-schedule
outputs.desc: An adjusted schedule based on your recall rate

outputs.name: retention-report
outputs.desc: A summary of retention and the changes made

process: Find items that lapse repeatedly and rewrite or split their prompts.
Adjust intervals that are too long or too short for your recall rate.
Retire items you no longer need to recall.
Summarize retention and the changes made.

description: Build a personal knowledge capture system where ideas are written in your own words, linked to related notes, stored with search and backlinks, and reviewed weekly so value compounds.

steps.description: Set up a reliable way to capture ideas the moment they occur.

inputs.name: knowledge-sources
inputs.desc: Where your ideas and inputs come from

inputs.name: tooling-constraints
inputs.desc: The tools and limits you will work within

outputs.name: capture-workflow
outputs.desc: A fast way to capture every new idea

outputs.name: inbox-location
outputs.desc: The single place new ideas first land

process: Choose a single inbox where every new idea first lands.
Define quick capture methods for each place ideas occur.
Set a rule that capture is fast and raw, not polished.
Confirm the capture step takes only a few seconds.

steps.description: Rewrite each captured item as a self-contained note in your own words.

inputs.name: capture-workflow

inputs.name: inbox-location
inputs.desc: The single place new ideas first land

outputs.name: atomic-notes

outputs.name: source-references
outputs.desc: The source recorded for each note

process: Restate each idea in your own words so it stands alone.
Keep one idea per note so it can be linked precisely.
Record the source reference for each note.
Give each note a title that states its idea.

steps.description: Link each note to related notes so ideas connect rather than sit in isolation.

inputs.name: source-references

outputs.name: linked-notes

Add two-way links and a short phrase describing the relationship.
Create entry notes that gather links to a cluster of ideas.

steps.description: Store notes so they are found through search and backlinks, not folder hierarchies.

inputs.name: linked-notes

inputs.name: link-map
inputs.desc: A map of how the notes connect

outputs.name: storage-scheme
outputs.desc: A scheme for storing and naming notes

outputs.name: retrieval-rules
outputs.desc: How notes are found when needed

process: Give each note a title that reads as a claim or question.
Rely on search and backlinks rather than deep folders.
Add tags only where they aid retrieval across clusters.
Test retrieval by finding a note three ways.

steps.description: Set up a weekly review that processes the inbox and strengthens links.

inputs.name: storage-scheme
inputs.desc: A scheme for storing and naming notes

inputs.name: retrieval-rules
inputs.desc: How notes are found when needed

outputs.name: weekly-review-checklist
outputs.desc: A checklist for the weekly review

outputs.name: review-cadence
outputs.desc: The fixed time and rhythm for the review

process: Process every item left in the inbox into a note or discard it.
Revisit recent notes and add any missing links.
Set the fixed weekly time and checklist for the review.
Note any cluster that is growing and worth attention.

steps.description: Track how the system compounds and surface clusters ready to become outputs.

inputs.name: weekly-review-checklist
inputs.desc: A checklist for the weekly review

inputs.name: review-cadence
inputs.desc: The fixed time and rhythm for the review

outputs.name: knowledge-system-map
outputs.desc: A map of how the system has grown

outputs.name: output-candidates
outputs.desc: Clusters ready to become an article, project, or decision

process: Watch which clusters of linked notes keep growing.
Flag clusters dense enough to turn into an article, project, or decision.
Record the system map and the candidate outputs.
Schedule a next step for the strongest candidate.

description: Learn a skill by building a real project: define a project that demands the skill, constrain its scope and timeline, and research just-in-time when you get stuck rather than studying everything up front.

inputs.name: skill-to-learn
inputs.desc: The skill you want to build

inputs.name: motivation-context
inputs.desc: Why you want it and how you will use it

outputs.name: skill-definition
outputs.desc: The skill stated in terms of what you can do

outputs.name: proof-criteria
outputs.desc: The evidence that would prove you have the skill

process: State the skill in terms of what you want to be able to do.
Define the observable evidence that would prove you can do it.
List the core sub-skills the project should exercise.
Confirm the proof criteria are checkable by someone else.

steps.description: Choose a concrete project that cannot be completed without using the skill.

inputs.name: skill-definition
inputs.desc: The skill stated in terms of what you can do

inputs.name: proof-criteria
inputs.desc: The evidence that would prove you have the skill

process: Brainstorm projects that force use of the target skill.
Pick one that is useful or interesting enough to finish.
Map which parts of the project exercise which sub-skills.

Define what is explicitly out of scope for this version.

inputs.name: deadline-plan
inputs.desc: A deadline short enough to force progress

outputs.name: milestone-plan
outputs.desc: Milestones that each end in a working piece

process: Split the project into milestones that each end in a working piece.
Order milestones so you build the hardest risky part early.
Define the very first build step you can start today.
Set a rough time estimate for each milestone.

steps.description: Research only when a build step blocks you, then return to building.

inputs.name: milestone-plan
inputs.desc: Milestones that each end in a working piece

inputs.name: first-build-step
inputs.desc: The very first step to start today

outputs.name: research-log
outputs.desc: A log of what you researched and learned

outputs.name: unblocked-steps

process: Start building and work until you hit a specific block.
Research the narrow question that unblocks the current step.
Return to building and log what you learned.

steps.description: Review the finished project against the proof criteria and plan the next build.

inputs.name: proof-criteria
inputs.desc: The evidence that would prove you have the skill

outputs.name: skill-evidence

Note which sub-skills are solid and which are still weak.

Ask the next specific question only once you have shown follow-through.

process: Name the specific skill or belief that no longer serves you.
Gather the evidence that it is outdated rather than merely uncomfortable.

Separate the pattern from any part still worth keeping.

steps.description: Understand why the old pattern exists and what it was once good for.
